findings.claim: Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get generated formatters and resolvers with no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`. The requirement asks for all generated code to be decorated. Its derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0, and class targets are valid there. The guard therefore drops the attribute on targets that support it, which includes most multi-targeted libraries. Ledger L5 says to follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedCodeExcludeFromCoverageLegacyTfmTests.GeneratedTypesAreExcludedOnLegacyTargets. It runs the generator with the NETSTANDARD2_0 and with the NETFRAMEWORK preprocessor symbol defined, then checks the generated formatter and resolver class declarations for the attribute. It fails on head because the attribute sits in an inactive #if region.

findings.claim: The README says the attribute is not available for `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework. That is factually wrong: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute ships in both. The docs therefore misstate why coverage exclusion is missing on those targets.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a netstandard2.0 class library and a net472 class library, each with `[System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] class C {}`. Both build, which contradicts README.md:1640.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Emit the attribute unconditionally, with no setting. Every generated formatter (int-key, string-key, enum, union) and every resolver, including its nested FormatterCache and GetFormatterHelper types, gets `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` behind a target-framework `#if`. Users cannot turn it off.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Same decoration, but with an opt-out setting as the requirement permits. Add a boolean option to GeneratorOptions, e.g. `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, defaulting to true and readable from the generator's existing options source (assembly attribute or analyzer config). Pass it to the templates. In each .tt/.cs template, write the `#if`/attribute lines only when the option is true. Add snapshot tests covering both settings and a README note describing the option.
